fr.elements: Main Building; Vehicle Parking Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Front Driveway; Internal Drive Aisle; Landscaped Area; Front Entry Area; Pedestrian Walkways; Street Frontage; Open Green Space
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Limited Rear Access; Dense Vegetation; Vehicle Congestion
fr.recommendations: Based on the observed site characteristics, multiple access points along the street frontage could support flexible responder positioning and apparatus placement during an incident. Addressing vehicle congestion within the parking areas and internal drive aisle would improve apparatus maneuvering and reduce potential delays in reaching the main building. Dense vegetation near landscaped areas and open green space may limit responder visibility and movement around the perimeter, and managing that vegetation could enhance situational awareness. Limited rear access may constrain apparatus positioning at the back of the structure, making familiarity with available approach routes from the front entry area particularly valuable for pre-incident planning.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Adjacent to Structure; Scattered Shrubs; Mixed Vegetation Cover; Irrigated Landscape; Brush Adjacent to Structure; Limited Defensible Space; Vegetation Adjacent to Access Route; Open Terrain
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing direct vegetation contact with structures and creating greater horizontal separation between shrub masses, tree clusters, and building perimeters could meaningfully improve defensible space and reduce fuel continuity across the property. Where brush and other vegetation are observed directly adjacent to structures, thinning or removing those fuels within the immediate structure zone would reduce the opportunity for surface fire to reach building surfaces. Managing the mixed and scattered vegetation across open terrain to increase spacing between individual plants and clusters may further reduce fuel continuity. Trimming lower limbs on trees within clusters could help separate surface and canopy fuels. Clearing and maintaining vegetation along the access route would support firefighter access and suppression operations during an incident. The existing irrigated landscape near structures represents a valuable fuel break that should be preserved and expanded where feasible, as maintained irrigated zones could improve defensible space and contribute to long-term wildfire resilience for the property.
